TX-2025892-HB22.policyArea: ALERT SYSTEM (S0523), BROADBAND DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (V62YT), COMPTROLLER OF PUBLIC ACCOUNTS (V2608)
TX-2025892-HB22.aiSummary: The bill would let the comptroller use a state fund to help pay for early warning systems and other emergency communication gear, including equipment, operations, and admin costs. It would also let the Broadband Development Office give contracts, grants, low-interest loans, and other help for these systems and for interoperable emergency communication equipment and infrastructure. The act would take effect on the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-SB14.title: Relating to the provision by a political subdivision of credits against impact fees to builders and developers for certain water conservation and reuse projects.

actions.text: Statement(s) of vote recorded in Journal
Reason for vote recorded in Journal
Comte report filed with Committee Coordinator
Received by the Secretary of the Senate

votes.motion: Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that SB 14 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-SB14.aiSummary: Local governments would have to give builders and developers credits against water and wastewater impact fees for certain projects that save, reuse, or reduce water use. The bill covers eligible facilities, systems, or products that cut water demand, lower wastewater needs, reduce stormwater needs, or meet stronger water-saving standards. Local governments would also have to set fair rules for figuring out and approving the credits. It takes effect January 1, 2026.

votes.motion: Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that HB 8 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-HB8.aiSummary: Texas HB 8 would change how public school tests are given and used for school accountability. It would move the state from STAAR to a new assessment program by the 2027-2028 school year, and it would require schools to give parents access to test results and notices through online portals. The bill would also change some test subjects, special education testing rules, and limits on using common core standards in state tests.

Senate Rule 7.18 and the Constitutional Rule requiring bills to be read on three several days be suspended and that SB 3 be placed on its third reading and final passage.

TX-2025892-SB3.aiSummary: The bill creates a state grant program to help cities, counties, and other local governments pay to install outdoor warning sirens in flash flood-prone areas. It also requires local governments in those areas to install, maintain, test, and operate sirens when the state board says they are needed, unless a working siren already meets state guidance. The law took effect immediately.

TX-2025892-SR70.title: In memory of Maxey Wayne Bruner of Longview.

actions.text: Received by the Secretary of the Senate

TX-2025892-SR70.aiSummary: This Senate resolution honors the memory of Maxey Wayne Bruner of Longview, who died on July 12, 2025, at age 90. It notes his Navy service, long career at Texas Eastman, faith, and family, and extends condolences to his relatives and friends. The Texas Senate adopted the resolution on September 4, 2025.

actions.text: Received by the Secretary of the Senate

TX-2025892-SR61.aiSummary: The Texas Senate resolution pays tribute to Jimmie Ruth Jaynes Ford of Jefferson after her death and offers condolences to her family and friends. It also asks for an official copy to be prepared for her family. The Senate adjourned that day in her memory.

TX-2025892-SR58.title: Recognizing the members of the Washington's Birthday Celebration Association for their planning of Washington's birthday celebration in Laredo.

actions.text: Received by the Secretary of the Senate

TX-2025892-SR58.policyArea: Resolutions--Congratulatory & Honorary (I0705), WASHINGTON'S BIRTHDAY CELEBRATION ASSOCIATION (N4913)
TX-2025892-SR58.aiSummary: The Senate adopted a resolution recognizing the members of the Washington's Birthday Celebration Association and its president for planning the annual Washington's birthday celebration in Laredo. It also notes that the celebration pays tribute to George Washington and that the 128th celebration will run from January 15 through February 28, 2026. A copy of the resolution would be prepared for the group as a sign of esteem from the Texas Senate.
